source_refs.source:
func hasType(type: int) -> bool:
	return type in descriptor.types or type in dynamicTypes

func canAffect(item):
	return item.hasType(Type.Food) and item.descriptor != descriptor

func hasType(type: int) -> bool:
	return type in ringTypes or .hasType(type)

argument: All six selected receiver kinds resolve canAffectDraggedItem/getAffectedCellsInInventory_cached/canAffect_color to Item. Neither the caller nor callees assign business fields/cache entries, call RNG, Timer, events or combat logs. Local variables and read-only array/dictionary membership checks do not mutate the sources.

Primary dynamic canAffect is false for Bag, Weapon and Shield chains; Potion calls target.hasType(Potion); Food calls target.hasType(Food) and descriptor comparison; King inherits Goobert, calling target.canActivate(). Secondary/tertiary/lightning resolve Item false in these selected chains.

Item.canActivate reads descriptor.canActivate. The Item-derived hasType override census finds only MagicRing.hasType, which reads ringTypes or delegates to pure base membership. Thus a global hovered/dragged target outside selected39 does not require proving it absent; these target queries remain read-only for original Item-derived targets.

Inventory.isHovered only checks curHovered membership; affectedCellsCache.get only returns an existing array/default empty array. No lazy caching or write occurs. focusItem.isBag is a constant false/true Item/Bag query.

The four booleans returned to Item._process select sprite.modulate only. Therefore arbitrary existing focusItem does not alter conditional business state/selected primitive consumption through this residual path.
limits: No assertion that Game.hoveredItems/draggedItem is empty or Game.state is Combat for the entire interval.
